evidence_profile.biological_context: Openly consented samples from people who declared themselves healthy, grouped by population label. The callsets describe germline variation in reference cohorts; no tissue, expression or phenotype data accompany the variants.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Observational genotype calls with sample and population metadata. No effect size or per-variant uncertainty is attached, and call quality differs between SNV, indel and SV callsets.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None for mechanism. Presence of an allele in a healthy-declared cohort is indirect evidence of tolerance only and cannot separate a benign allele from one with recessive, late-onset or reduced-penetrance effects.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Observation in healthy-declared individuals argues against a high-penetrance, early-onset dominant effect of that allele; it does not exclude recessive, late-onset or reduced-penetrance effects.
evidence_profile.absence_means: An allele missing from the callset was not observed in this cohort. Coverage, callset design and population representation decide what could be seen; absence is not evidence of rarity or harm.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Predicts a pathogenicity class for single amino-acid substitutions per transcript or isoform. No tissue, cell-type, dosage, inheritance or mechanism context is carried.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Computational prediction. Class thresholds were chosen to reach 90% precision on ClinVar labels although the model was not trained on ClinVar variants, so agreement with ClinVar is calibration and not independent confirmation. No per-variant uncertainty is provided.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low. The score does not say whether a change causes loss or gain of function, destabilisation or a dominant-negative effect, and it cannot see effects that act through splicing or regulation.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A pathogenicity likelihood for the substitution; no phenotype, penetrance or mode of inheritance.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No score exists for synonymous, nonsense, splice, indel, structural or non-coding variants. Absence of a prediction is not evidence of a benign effect.

sources.name: BioGRID protein and genetic interactions (release 5.0.262, human file)

version.value: BioGRID release 5.0.262 (read from the member names of the organism archive fetched on 2026-10-25; the "Latest-Release" archive is generated on request)

sources.scope: Literature-curated interactions in tab3 format. The human file holds 1,433,067 interactions: 1,411,994 physical and 21,073 genetic, from 29 experimental systems (genetic ones include synthetic lethality, synthetic rescue, dosage rescue, dosage lethality, positive and negative genetic interaction, phenotypic enhancement and suppression, synthetic growth defect). 1,319,164 (92%) are human-human; the rest are cross-species and host-pathogen interactions, mainly SARS-CoV-2, mouse, rat, HIV-1, HPV and yeast proteins with a human partner. The archive holds 98 organism files; only the human file is used.
sources.mapping_methods: Each interaction names both partners by Entrez Gene id, symbol and UniProt/RefSeq accessions, plus the experimental system, system type (physical or genetic), throughput, author and PubMed id of the supporting publication.

quantitative.summary: Presence of an interaction with its experimental system and throughput; an optional score for some systems.
quantitative.uncertainty: throughput (high or low) and number of supporting publications, not a probability
quantitative.direction: n/a for physical interactions; genetic systems encode the direction (for example negative or positive genetic)

licence.name: MIT License: "100% freely available to both academic and commercial users" and provided without warranty (BioGRID download repository page, verified live); citation of the contributing authors and the BioGRID publication is requested.
licence.redistribution: MIT terms

sources.update_frequency: Monthly releases (the release number advances with each).
coverage_limitations: Interactions are curated from publications and reflect what has been studied; well-studied proteins have many more interactions
Physical interactions say two proteins were found together in an assay (system types such as affinity capture or two-hybrid differ in what that means), not that they interact in a given tissue
Genetic interactions are mostly from yeast and from screens in cell lines; 21,073 are in the human file
About 8% of the human file are cross-species or host-pathogen interactions and must not be read as human-human

Interactions of IntAct, STRING and Reactome are held through Open Targets (interaction dataset)

reuse_decision.rationale: The only open resource in the catalogue that carries curated genetic interactions (synthetic lethality, dosage rescue, suppression) for epistasis and compensation, alongside physical interactions; MIT-licensed and a single 189 MB archive. Open Targets already integrates IntAct, STRING, Reactome and Signor interactions, so those are not mirrored separately.

status.notes: Archive generated on request: no size or checksum is published, so the manifest pins size and SHA-256; the release number is read from the member names.

unverified_fields: update frequency (monthly releases are stated on the BioGRID site, not retrieved here)

mechanism_evidence.note: curated genetic interactions from double-perturbation experiments; whole-gene, not allele-specific

components.name: physical interactions (affinity capture, two-hybrid and related systems)
genetic interactions (synthetic lethality, dosage rescue, suppression and related systems)

evidence_profile.biological_context: Interactions from published experiments in many systems (cell lines, yeast and others); each row records the experimental system, throughput and publication. The partner proteins are whole proteins, so an interaction is not tied to a particular isoform, domain or variant.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Curated from the literature; the supporting publications and experimental systems are the evidence, and high-throughput studies are flagged. Counts of supporting publications are an indication of reproducibility, not a probability.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate. A genetic interaction shows that perturbing two genes together has an effect that differs from the single perturbations, which is the basis for epistasis and compensation hypotheses; it does not identify the allele, the pathway step or the direction of compensation. A physical interaction does not show that a variant disrupts it.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Cell-level or organism-level phenotype of the double perturbation, as described in the supporting study; no human disease phenotype.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A missing interaction means it was not reported in curated publications, which reflects what has been tested; it does not show that two genes do not interact, nor that perturbing both has no combined effect.

overlaps_with_sources.note: Open Targets interactions come from IntAct, Signor, Reactome and STRING; BioGRID is a separate curation, so the same pair can appear in both and should be counted once per publication

evidence_profile.biological_context: Expert-panel curation of whole genes and genomic regions: dosage sensitivity (loss or gain of an entire gene or region), recurrent CNV regions and gene-disease validity. Gene- and region-level assertions; recurrent regions are intervals.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Graded by curators from published cases. Dosage scores encode evidence levels; 30 stands for a gene associated with an autosomal recessive phenotype and 40 for dosage sensitivity unlikely. A curated judgement, not a measurement, and not allele-specific.

evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene or region without a record has not been curated, which differs from a score meaning no evidence (0) or dosage sensitivity unlikely (40). Absence is not evidence of dosage tolerance.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Each score is a weighted sum of effect-allele dosages from a published model, developed for a stated trait in stated development samples and evaluated in other samples; ancestry and cohort come with the score.

evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Predisposition to a trait in the ancestry the score was developed and evaluated in. A raw score is meaningful only against a reference distribution of the same score and ancestry.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant that is not a weight of a score was not selected or estimated by that model. Absence from a score is not evidence of no effect, and a missing genotype is not a zero dosage.

mechanism_evidence.note: variant-drug annotations with levels of evidence

evidence_profile.biological_context: Annotations linking variants, haplotypes, genes and drugs from published studies. Each annotation records the studied variant or haplotype, the drug, a phenotype category, the population and a level of evidence.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Literature-derived annotations with levels of evidence for clinical annotations. Individual studies are small and often conflict, and the annotation level is not an effect size.

mechanism_evidence.note: defining variants of star alleles; function is assigned elsewhere

evidence_profile.biological_context: Nomenclature and defining variants for star alleles of 15 pharmacogenes, on RefSeqGene, GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates. Structural variation and complex variant types are described separately from sequence haplotypes.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Consortium-curated nomenclature. An allele definition lists the variants that define a haplotype; a name is a definition and not evidence of function.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Not applicable to function. A star allele defines which variants occur together; function and drug response are assigned by other resources (CPIC, PharmGKB) and the mechanism of each variant is not given.

evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant not in any allele definition is not a named allele, so its function is unassigned and not normal. Genes outside the 15 are not covered.

sources.name: ProteinGym v1.3: deep mutational scanning benchmark assays (substitutions and indels)
sources.maintainer: ProteinGym project (OATML-Markslab repository; files served from marks.hms.harvard.edu)

version.value: v1.3 (files dated 2025-04-13); the repository README lists releases v1.0 to v1.3

sources.scope: Curated deep mutational scanning benchmark: 217 substitution assays (2,465,767 variants, 96 on human proteins, 69 including multiple mutants) and 66 indel assays (287,207 variants, 25 on human proteins) from published studies, each as a table of variants with the measured score and a binarised label, plus a reference file with the target sequence, organism, publication and selection assay of every assay. The clinical benchmarks, model scores, alignments and structures of the project are not fetched.
identifiers: amino-acid substitution strings relative to the assay target sequence (multiple mutants joined by colons)
DMS assay id (UniProt entry name, first author, year)
sources.mapping_methods: Mutations are given relative to the target sequence stored in the reference file; every substitution row was checked to apply to that sequence and to reproduce the mutated sequence. The UniProt entry name is the only protein identifier, so joins to UniProt accessions, transcripts or genome coordinates need a separate mapping. Indel assays give only the mutated sequence.

quantitative.summary: Per-variant assay score in the units of the source experiment, and a 0/1 label obtained with a per-assay cutoff.
quantitative.units: assay-specific; the direction of the score differs between assays and is recorded in the reference file
quantitative.uncertainty: none per variant (replicate statistics are not retained)
quantitative.direction: assay-specific; higher usually means higher fitness, with the raw directionality recorded per assay

licence.name: MIT licence for the ProteinGym project (LICENSE of the OATML-Markslab/ProteinGym repository, read in the read-only clone at commit 144fe22). The licences of the underlying published assay datasets are not stated in the repository files.
licence.redistribution: MIT terms for the project; the original studies' terms may apply to their data

sources.update_frequency: Versioned releases (v1.0 to v1.3 in the repository README).
coverage_limitations: A curated subset of published assays chosen for benchmarking models, not an exhaustive collection of deep mutational scans
Scores are assay-specific and not harmonised; no per-variant uncertainty is retained
Variants are amino-acid changes in the assay construct, which may be a fragment or domain; no nucleotide or genome coordinates are given
Many assays measure stability by cDNA display proteolysis rather than function; the selection type is recorded per assay
Only 96 of the 217 substitution assays and 25 of the 66 indel assays are on human proteins
known_omissions: The clinical benchmarks (labels derived from clinical databases) are not fetched; the clinical records are held through ClinVar
Zero-shot and supervised model scores, multiple sequence alignments and weights, predicted structures and cross-validation splits are not fetched
Raw (unprocessed) assay files are not fetched

reuse_decision.rationale: An established curated benchmark that already puts 283 published assays into one checked format; reusing it avoids re-curating each paper. Some assays are expected to be the same experiments as MaveDB score sets, so they are matched by publication and target before any combination, and each experiment is counted once.

status.notes: Plain HTTPS downloads; the server publishes no checksum, so sizes are pinned and zip integrity is tested. One assay file carries an extra DMS_bin_score column.

unverified_fields: licences of the underlying published assay datasets
which assays are the same experiments as MaveDB score sets (not yet matched)

mechanism_evidence.note: assay-specific readout such as growth, binding, abundance or proteolytic stability
assays with multiple mutants allow non-additivity (epistasis) to be estimated

components.name: published deep mutational scanning measurements, re-formatted

evidence_profile.biological_context: Each assay measures a variant library of one protein or domain in a specific system; the organism, selection assay and selection type are given per assay in the reference file. The score reflects the assayed function under that selection.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurements curated and processed by the benchmark maintainers: scores are as published in assay-specific units and the binarised label uses a per-assay cutoff. Replicate-level uncertainty is not retained.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the assayed molecular function of the substitution in the assayed system. Stability, activity and binding effects are not separated unless the selection type says so.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A molecular or cellular phenotype of the assay. Correspondence to a human disease phenotype needs calibration, and most assays are of non-human proteins or of protein stability.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A mutation missing from an assay table was not measured or was filtered by the maintainers; an untested position is unknown and not tolerant. A protein with no assay has no curated measurement here.

overlaps_with_sources.note: some assays are the same experiments as MaveDB score sets; match by publication and target before combining, and count each experiment once

Does not encode epistasis or compensation quantitatively

sources.name: NCBI RefSeq: GRCh38.p14 accession map, alternate-locus placement and gene annotation (release RS_2025_08)

version.value: GCF_000001405.40 (GRCh38.p14) with annotation release GCF_000001405.40-RS_2025_08 (annotation software 10.4, evidence freeze 01-August-2025, release 06-August-2025); the annotation_releases listing shows RS_2025_08 as the current release

sources.scope: The RefSeq view of GRCh38.p14: the assembly report that maps every sequence between RefSeq, GenBank and UCSC-style names and gives its role (assembled molecule, alternate scaffold, fix or novel patch, unlocalised or unplaced scaffold); the named regions that carry alternate loci or patches; the placement of each alternate-locus and patch scaffold on the chromosomes; and the RefSeq annotation of genes, transcripts (NM_, NR_, XM_, XR_), exons and CDS in GFF3, made by the NCBI eukaryotic annotation pipeline (Best-placed RefSeq, Gnomon, RefSeqFE, cmsearch, tRNAscan-SE).
identifiers: RefSeq accessions (NC_, NT_, NW_, NM_, NR_, XM_, XR_)
sources.mapping_methods: The assembly report gives RefSeq accession, GenBank accession, sequence name and UCSC-style name for each sequence, which is how contig names used by ClinVar (RefSeq NT_/NW_), Ensembl (sequence names) and GIAB (chr names) are tied together; the GFF3 carries GeneID and HGNC cross-references per gene.

quantitative.summary: Sequence and feature annotation; no scores.

licence.name: NCBI data usage policy: NCBI places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the data in its databases; original submitters may claim rights; acknowledgement of NLM is requested (NCBI Policies and Disclaimers page). RefSeq-specific terms were not separately retrieved.
licence.redistribution: No NCBI restriction; third-party submitter rights may apply

sources.update_frequency: Annotation releases roughly yearly for GRCh38.p14 (the listing shows RS_2023_03, RS_2023_10, RS_2024_08 and RS_2025_08); the assembly itself changes only with a new patch release.
coverage_limitations: GRCh38.p14 only; the T2T-CHM13v2.0 RefSeq annotation (GCF_009914755.1) is listed by NCBI but not fetched
The annotation is NCBI's own gene set: it differs from the Ensembl and GENCODE gene sets in transcripts, boundaries and identifiers; MANE Select pairs one transcript of each
Placements on alternate loci and patches repeat genes of the primary assembly, so feature counts are larger than counts of distinct genes
known_omissions: Genome, transcript and protein sequence files (genomic.fna 928 MB, rna, protein, gbff), the GTF, feature table, repeat annotation output (rm.out) and the per-scaffold alignments are not fetched
Annotation_comparison files and the annotation report are not fetched

The 80 KB report, 45 KB regions file and 78 MB GFF are small relative to their use; sequence files are not needed because the Ensembl FASTA is mirrored.

status.notes: FTP files with MD5 checksums published in md5checksums.txt; all six files verified against them.

mechanism_evidence.note: RefSeq transcript structures on which ClinVar HGVS is expressed
alternate-locus and patch scaffolds and the regions they cover

evidence_profile.biological_context: Reference accessions and transcript models of one haploid reference with alternate loci and patches. The annotation is a set of transcript models and not a map of which isoform is expressed where.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Reference data from an automated and curated annotation pipeline; correctness is checked here by published checksums, structural consistency of the GFF and joins to the other reference files.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Not applicable. It supplies identifiers, roles and transcript structure needed to define consequences and to recognise regions with competing representations; it asserts no effect.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None: accession maps and gene models carry no phenotype information.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A sequence not in the report is not part of GRCh38.p14; a position outside annotated features is not shown to be non-functional; a region without alternate loci or patches is not shown to be free of duplication.

overlaps_with_sources.note: MANE Select pairs one RefSeq with one Ensembl transcript per gene; the RefSeq half of MANE should reappear in this annotation, and the two gene sets are otherwise independent annotations of the same genome
independent annotation of the same assembly; compare transcript sets and boundaries, never merge counts

sources.name: STRchive and related tandem-repeat catalogues
sources.maintainer: STRchive (Dashnow lab, University of Colorado, and collaborators)

version.value: Site v2.28.0; 82 disease loci

sources.scope: Curated tandem-repeat loci associated with Mendelian disease with hg38/hg19/T2T coordinates and catalogues for TRGT, ExpansionHunter-style, atarva, longTR, straglr and Stranger. The resources page also points to gnomAD tandem repeats, PlatinumTRs (7.8 million reference TRs) and STRipy.
sources.mapping_methods: Locus definitions per assembly; breadth chosen to allow interruptions (site notes that definitions differ between resources).

licence.redistribution: Attribution

coverage_limitations: Disease loci only; genome-wide repeat catalogues are separate resources
Locus definitions differ across catalogues
known_omissions: Population allele-size distributions are in gnomAD TR (not acquired)

reuse_decision.rationale: Small, openly licensed disease-locus catalogue. Catalogue files are linked for download from the STRchive site itself (hosted as raw files on GitHub).

status.notes: Site pages rendered; download links extracted.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Curated tandem-repeat loci associated with Mendelian disease: locus coordinates (hg38, hg19, T2T-CHM13), repeat motif and locus structure, inheritance mode, and normal and pathogenic length thresholds.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Expert curation from the literature. Thresholds differ between loci and are summarised as single numbers; intermediate ranges, repeat interruptions and somatic instability are not captured by one threshold.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for repeat length and motif as the disease-relevant variable at curated loci. The molecular mechanism (RNA toxicity, polyglutamine proteotoxicity, silencing) varies by locus and is not resolved by length alone.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Length above the pathogenic threshold associates with the named disease; onset, penetrance and severity depend on length and modifiers.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A locus missing from the catalogue is not curated as disease-associated. It is not shown to be benign, and the catalogue covers only loci with published disease associations.

sources.name: STRING protein-protein association networks

quantitative.summary: Combined association score from channels (experiments, databases, text mining, co-expression, neighbourhood, fusion, co-occurrence).
quantitative.uncertainty: the score is a confidence, not a measured strength

licence.name: CC BY 4.0 as listed for STRING in the Open Targets data-source licence table; the STRING licence page itself was not read.
licence.redistribution: Attribution; STRING terms not read

coverage_limitations: A STRING link is an association (including text mining and co-expression), not necessarily a physical interaction
Scores are confidences and depend on channel weights
known_omissions: All files: the association scores reach the library through the Open Targets interaction dataset; the full-network files are far too large and the human-only files were not fetched

reuse_decision.rationale: Already integrated in Open Targets (13.2 million rows, 6.5 million distinct gene pairs), and the full network is 124.6 GB. A human-only file could be fetched later if channel subscores are needed.

evidence_profile.evidence_strength: A mixture of curated, experimental and predicted evidence combined into a confidence; the channels differ greatly in reliability.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low. It places proteins in a network; it does not show that a variant affects a link.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A pair without a link has no combined evidence above the stored threshold; it is not shown to be unrelated.

sources.name: TRExplorer: genome-wide tandem-repeat catalogue

licence.name: Not found: neither the about page, the FAQ nor the bucket listing states a data licence.
licence.redistribution: Unknown

The annotated tables are very large

mechanism_evidence.note: polymorphism of repeat loci in long-read genomes

evidence_profile.biological_context: Repeat loci defined from the reference sequence with motifs, annotated with polymorphism in assembled genomes of diverse ancestry (HPRC).

mechanism_evidence.note: function, domain, site and modification annotations

components.name: sequence, function, domain, site and modification annotation

evidence_profile.biological_context: Reviewed (Swiss-Prot) human protein entries with literature-curated annotation. Annotations refer to the canonical sequence, and isoforms are described by their differences.
